claim_verdicts.evidence: Key shell fits. Bash 5.3 manual 3.7.1/3.7.2: a simple command is 'a command name and an optional list of arguments'; 3.5.7 splitting applies only to unquoted expansion results, 'Words that were not expanded are not split'. Prior execution r2: `ls -1 db docs www | cat -A` showed each operand reached ls as typed.

Key shell fits. Bash 5.3 manual 3.7.2 Command Search and Execution: 'If the name does not match a function, the shell searches for it in the list of shell builtins. If a match is found, that builtin is invoked. If the name is neither a shell function nor a builtin, and contains no slashes, Bash searches each element of $PATH'. cd is listed under 4.1 Bourne Shell Builtins. Prior r2: `type -t` -> cd builtin, ls/cat/... file.

Key shell fits. Bash 5.3 manual 4.1 cd: 'Change the current working directory to directory.' 3.7.3: a non-builtin command 'is invoked in a separate execution environment', so its directory change is its own. Prior execution r2: `cd /; bash -c "cd /repo/db && pwd"; pwd` -> /repo/db then /.

Key shell fits. Bash 5.3 manual 3.7.2: 'Bash searches each element of $PATH for a directory containing an executable file by that name'; then the shell 'executes the named program in a separate execution environment'; 'If the command was not begun asynchronously, the shell waits for the command to complete and collects its exit status.' Prior execution r2 matched.

Linux and Git Bash halves documented: coreutils manual has sections for ls (10.1), cat, mkdir (12.3), cp, mv, rm, pwd; bash 4.1 lists cd and pwd as builtins; r2 resolved all eight in the lab box and Git Bash. macOS ships BSD utilities, not GNU coreutils, so key coreutils does not govern the macOS half and no macOS docs root exists. Kind fact, not blocking.

Key shell fits. Bash 5.3 manual 8.4.6 complete (TAB): 'Attempt to perform completion on the text before point. ... Bash attempts completion by first checking for any programmable completions for the command word, otherwise treating the text as a' filename etc. Prior r2: compgen -d qu -> queries; xyz -> nothing; mode-000 folder still completes. 'or several do, nothing is filled in' is too broad (shared longer prefix gets filled). Note: Tab runs in Git Bash (bash 5.2.26), not the pinned 5.3.
claim_verdicts.source: gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html (Edition 5.3), 8.4.6 Commands For Completion; execution r2
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: In bash (the shell Git Bash opens and the one the lab box runs), Tab completes a partly typed name from the names the shell can see from where it stands; if no name starts with the typed text, nothing is filled in. A folder completes by name even if the user may not enter it.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Key shell fits. Bash 5.3 manual 8.4.2 previous-history (C-p): 'Move back through the history list, fetching the previous command. This may also be bound to the up arrow key on some keyboards.' Prior r2: Git Bash and lab box `bind -p` -> "\e[A": previous-history; `set -o` -> history on.
claim_verdicts.source: gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html (Edition 5.3), 8.4.2, 9 Bash History Facilities; execution r2

claim_verdicts.evidence: Key coreutils fits. Coreutils 10.1 ls: '-1 List one file per line.' Directory headings with multiple operands are not spelled out in the mirror text I opened; decisive is prior execution r2 in the lab box: `ls -1 db docs www | cat -A` -> `db:$ queries$ ... $ docs:$ ...`, operand name as heading, groups separated by an empty line.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/web/coreutils.html (GNU Coreutils 9.12; pin 9.11) 10.1 ls; execution r2

claim_verdicts.evidence: Key coreutils fits. Coreutils 6.1 wc: 'wc prints one line of counts for each file, and if the file was given as an argument, it prints the file name following the counts.' `git show stage-0:db/schema.sql | wc -l` -> 48; lesson line `48 db/schema.sql` matches stage-0 tour.txt (r2).

Key coreutils fits. Coreutils 5.1 head: '-n [-]num ... Output the first num lines'; 'For compatibility head also supports an obsolete option syntax -[num]...', which `head -2` is. Prior r2: select-basics.sql has 19 lines and the tour output holds only the first two.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/web/coreutils.html (GNU Coreutils 9.12; pin 9.11) 5.1 head; execution r2

claim_verdicts.evidence: Key shell fits. Bash 5.3 manual 4.2 echo: 'Output the args, separated by spaces, terminated with a newline.' No args -> just the newline. Prior r2: `echo | od -c` -> single \n; stage-0 tour.txt holds four blank lines from bare echo and two from ls.
claim_verdicts.source: gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html (Edition 5.3), 4.2 echo; stage-0 tour.txt; execution r2
